channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbek Diplomat Mirvokhid Azimov Appointed Secretary General of Turkic States Organization
item.description: Uzbek diplomat Mirvokhid Azimov has been appointed the new Secretary General of the Organization of Turkic States (OTS), becoming the first Uzbek to hold the position. The decision was made at the 13th OTS summit in Ankara. Azimov previously served as Deputy Secretary General and Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs.

item.title: New Prosecutor's Office with AI Assistant Opens in Kosshy, Kazakhstan
item.description: A new city prosecutor's office equipped with an AI assistant has opened in Kosshy, Kazakhstan. The AI system allows citizens to book appointments, track the status of their appeals, and obtain necessary information. The office also presented digital oversight programs and a city-wide video surveillance system.

item.title: Turkmenistan Celebrates 33rd Anniversary of National Currency Introduction
item.description: Turkmenistan is celebrating the 33rd anniversary of the introduction of its national currency, the manat. The currency's introduction is credited with ensuring stable economic development, effective monetary policy, and increased lending to various sectors. The manat plays a crucial role in regulating money supply and attracting investment.

item.title: Taliban Beat Mosque Imam in Panjshir for Violating Curfew
item.description: Sources in Panjshir report that the Taliban assaulted a mosque imam, Mullah Abdul Farooq Zahir, during morning prayers in the Darah district. The imam was reportedly beaten for violating the Taliban's strict night-time curfew, which prohibits movement from 7 PM to dawn. The Taliban have imposed severe restrictions on Panjshir residents.

item.title: Finland's President: Putin Call Made at Ukraine's Request for Dialogue
item.description: Finnish President Alexander Stubb stated that a phone call with Vladimir Putin, also involving the Norwegian Prime Minister, was initiated at Ukraine's request to facilitate dialogue between Kyiv and Moscow. Stubb clarified that Finland was not acting as a mediator but aimed to establish a communication channel. The call occurred on October 27.

item.title: Iran's top security official received US letter, has not yet responded
item.description: Mohsen Rezaei, Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary, stated he read a letter from US Deputy President J.D. Vance but has not yet replied. Rezaei claimed the letter's tone indicated a significant shift, which he viewed positively for Iran's established power. He mentioned the US had not disclosed the letter's contents, thus he would not reveal them either. Mediators delivered the letter to Tehran last Sunday.

item.title: Taliban report 135 shops destroyed in Mazar-e-Sharif market fire
item.description: The Taliban announced that 135 shops were destroyed in a fire at the Bakhtar underground market in Mazar-e-Sharif. The fire, which broke out on Friday, caused millions of dollars in damage. The Taliban cited electrical short circuits and negligence as possible causes, also noting the market's substandard construction and lack of fire prevention measures contributed to the blaze.

item.title: Iran Shortens Strait of Hormuz Reopening Plan Timeline to Two Days
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi announced that Iran has reduced the timeline for its Strait of Hormuz reopening plan to two days. Iran wants ships to use only the agreed shipping route with Oman, keeping other routes closed. This could facilitate renewed negotiations with the US on outstanding issues.

item.title: Germany's Generation Z Demands Chancellor Merz's Resignation
item.description: Generation Z in Germany is protesting, with some participants dressed in costumes and others carrying GDR flags and communist symbols. They are demanding the resignation of Chancellor Friedrich Merz. Protests are occurring in several cities, with participants calling for climate action, lower living costs, and increased school funding.

item.title: Syria in Talks to Join 'Makkah Treaty' Defense Pact
item.description: Syrian Foreign Minister Assaad Shubaani stated that Damascus is in discussions to join the 'Makkah Treaty,' a defense agreement between Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan. Shubaani emphasized Syria's role in regional security and the need for joint defense systems. The treaty considers an attack on one member as an attack on all.

item.title: 17-Year-Old Killed in Mortar Shell Explosion in Afghanistan's Ghazni Province
item.description: A 17-year-old shepherd named Mohammad Akbar died from a mortar shell explosion in Badr village, Ab Band District, Ghazni Province. The incident occurred when the youth ignited the shell. This follows a similar fatal mortar shell explosion involving a child in Nangarhar Province three days prior.

item.title: Canada and European Union Agree to Form New Alliance
item.description: Canada and the European Union have agreed to establish a strategic partnership. The initiative aims to strengthen ties in foreign policy and security, remove trade barriers, and boost digital market development and critical mineral supply.

item.title: Iran Warns US and Israel of Massive Response to Any Attack
item.description: Iran's Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces warned the United States and Israel of a massive and unimaginable response to any attack. He stated that Iran has identified new enemy targets and would determine the end of any potential new war.

item.title: Analysis Examines Political Intelligence and Foreign Dependence of Afghan Politicians
item.description: An analysis suggests understanding Afghan politicians' mindset is key to grasping the nation's condition, noting politics there deviates from global norms, centering on traditionalism and foreign influence. Afghan governments historically operated under external powers, making individual merit secondary to securing foreign backing, leading to instability.

item.title: Tirzetta Drug Based on Tirzepatide Launched in Kazakhstan
item.description: The Russian company 'Promomed' has launched the drug 'Tirzetta' (INN - tirzepatide) in Kazakhstan. The launch occurred at a forum discussing metabolic health, attended by endocrinologists from Kazakhstan and Russia. The drug is registered in Kazakhstan, highlighting the healthcare system's recognition of this drug class's importance.

item.title: Taliban Arrest Three Panjshir Residents in Kabul, Including Ex-Military
item.description: Sources report the Taliban have arrested three residents from Panjshir province in Kabul, two of whom are former security force members. Wahidullah Bahaduri, previously imprisoned by the Taliban, was rearrested five days ago. Agha Shirin was arrested two days prior in Dehmazang. Zakaria, another Panjshir resident, was also detained.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Malik Shavaev Wins Bronze at World Wrestling Championships
item.description: Kyrgyz athlete Malik Shavaev secured a bronze medal at the World Wrestling Championships in Astana, Kazakhstan. Competing in the 86 kg weight category, Shavaev defeated Ibrahim Kadiyev of Russia for the bronze. Earlier, he beat athletes from Puerto Rico, Switzerland, and Iran.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ministry Clarifies Rules on Fining Employees for Lateness
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Labor and Social Protection has clarified that employers cannot legally impose monetary fines on employees for lateness or other minor disciplinary infractions. While employers can issue warnings or reprimands, financial penalties not specified in the Labor Code are prohibited without written employee consent.

item.title: Man Arrested in Shymkent for Allegedly Defrauding 292 Investors of 4 Billion Tenge
item.description: A 45-year-old man, wanted internationally, has been arrested in Shymkent. He is accused of collecting over 4 billion tenge from 292 individuals, promising to build a residential complex in Astana. The Ministry of Internal Affairs reported that construction proceeded without necessary permits or state expert review.

item.title: Environmental Fines Exceed 371 Million Tenge in East Kazakhstan
item.description: In East Kazakhstan, environmental violators have been fined over 371.5 million tenge following inspections. 167 administrative protocols were issued, and 66 orders to eliminate violations were given. Of the fines, 135 have been collected, with 32 outstanding payments totaling 135.7 million tenge. "Kaztsink" faced significant fines for emissions and operational violations.

item.title: Iran Carefully Reviewing US Letter, Sees Positive Step for Dialogue
item.description: Iran's Foreign Minister stated that a letter from US Vice President Kamala Harris to Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary has been carefully reviewed. He described the US effort to open broader dialogue as a positive step, but warned against attempts to create division. No meeting between US and Iranian officials is currently planned.

item.title: Poland's President returns amid escalating constitutional court crisis
item.description: Poland is facing a severe political and judicial crisis centered on a dispute between Prime Minister Donald Tusk's government and President Andrzej Duda concerning the Constitutional Tribunal. Protests erupted in Warsaw as a judge attempted to suspend tribunal leadership, leading to clashes with police.

item.title: Tajik Citizens Imprisoned in Russia Appeal for Help from Dushanbe
item.description: Tajik citizens serving sentences in a Volgograd prison claim they are under severe pressure from staff to sign contracts with the Russian Ministry of Defense. They have appealed to Tajik authorities to facilitate their return to their home country, expressing fear for their lives.

item.title: Foreign National Dies Near Semey Court in Case Involving 19.9 Million Tenge Dispute
item.description: A foreign national, who was a victim in a criminal case, died near the Semey regional court on October 30. The case involved a dispute over five dump trucks and a claim for 19.9 million tenge in damages. Police are investigating the incident, which may have been self-immolation.

item.title: Poland's Constitutional Tribunal Building Surrounded by Police Amid Judicial Dispute
item.description: Police surrounded Poland's Constitutional Tribunal building in Warsaw after a judge suspended its president and vice-president. The judge cited obstruction of justice. The tribunal's website claims the court was "hijacked," while police stated they were responding to a potential threat. Protesters gathered, and three arrests were made.

item.title: Kazakhstan Seizes Nearly 12 Kilograms of Drugs in Caspian Sea Operations
item.description: Kazakhstan's Border Service has seized approximately 11.5 kilograms of narcotics during operations in the Caspian Sea. The agency also confiscated 88 kilometers of illegal fishing gear and released 2,337 sturgeon and other fish back into their natural habitat. Fines totaling over 4.5 million tenge were imposed.

item.title: MP: New Draft of Bishkek's General Plan Not Yet Published
item.description: A Member of Parliament stated that while the Cabinet of Ministers has amended Bishkek's General Plan until 2050, the updated master drawing has not been published. The document, which defines the capital's functional zones, was published without the revised drawing, and public discussion information is missing.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans to Build 112 New Schools and 40 Hospitals by 2027
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to construct 112 new schools and 40 hospitals by 2027 as part of ongoing social infrastructure improvements. The Speaker of the Jogorku Kenesh highlighted significant development under President Sadyr Japarov, noting the construction of 700 educational facilities and 500 factories in the past five years.

item.title: CSTO Operation 'Channel - Caspian Beacon' Seizes Drugs, Weapons, and Crypto
item.description: The CSTO's anti-narcotics operation 'Channel - Caspian Beacon' concluded, targeting drug trafficking and criminal groups. Authorities seized narcotics, psychotropic substances, weapons, and ammunition. The operation also uncovered cryptocurrency schemes and identified online platforms used for drug propaganda. It involved law enforcement, border, and customs agencies from CSTO member states, along with Iran and China.

item.title: Afghanistan's Taliban Spokesperson: Pakistan Unwilling to Resolve Tensions Through Dialogue
item.description: Zabihullah Mujahid, spokesperson for Afghanistan's Islamic Emirate, stated that Kabul's efforts to resolve tensions with Pakistan through dialogue have failed. He attributed the lack of progress to Pakistan's 'wrong policies,' asserting that Islamabad shows little willingness for peaceful negotiations. Mujahid reiterated Afghanistan's commitment to resolving disputes diplomatically, despite ongoing bilateral tensions.

item.title: Badakhshan Governor Urges Youth to Reject Opposition and Foster National Unity
item.description: Badakhshan Governor Rahmatullah Najib called on Afghan youth to reject foreign propaganda and opposition groups, emphasizing national unity and an end to violence. He described the current system as a shared home for all Afghans and warned against armed activities not sanctioned as legitimate jihad.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Select Military Food Service Companies via Tender for 2027-2028
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Defense plans to hold a state tender to select companies that will provide catering services for military personnel in 2027-2028. The tender process will be conducted through the State Procurement Center, with details to be announced on the Kazakhstan State Procurement Web Portal.

item.title: Kazakh President Proposes Russia Observer Status in Turkic States Organization
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev proposed considering Russia's participation in the Organization of Turkic States (OTS) as an observer or through an "OTS+" format. This initiative, made during the 13th OTS summit in Ankara, aims to leverage historical ties and strengthen Eurasian cooperation without opposing integration processes.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Singapore to Enhance Technical Cooperation in Civil Aviation
item.description: Kazakhstan's Aviation Administration (KAA) and Singapore's Civil Aviation Authority (CAAS) signed a Statement of Intent to expand technical partnership, covering flight safety, risk-based oversight, personnel training, and sustainable development. This agreement broadens cooperation beyond existing training programs, with a new MoU planned for 2027.

item.title: Tajikistan Mandates Fortification of Flour and Iodization of Salt from September
item.description: Starting September 1st, Tajikistan will require premium and first-grade wheat flour intended for the domestic market to be sold only in fortified form. The new regulations also mandate the iodization of salt. These measures aim to improve public health and nutrition across the country.

item.title: Uzbekistan Senate Holds Seminar on Increasing Local Budget Revenues and Reducing Shadow Economy
item.description: The Senate of Uzbekistan's Committee on Budget and Economic Issues organized a seminar for local deputies on enhancing local budget revenues and curbing the shadow economy. Discussions focused on regional financial autonomy, tax administration improvements, and strengthening parliamentary oversight.

item.title: Illegally Constructed Emergency Ministry Building Demolished at Baitik Weather Station
item.description: An illegally constructed building belonging to the Ministry of Emergency Situations has been demolished at the Baitik weather station in Kyrgyzstan. The structure was built within the water protection zone of the Ala-Archa River. The former minister of emergency situations was prosecuted, and the state's losses were compensated.

item.title: Large Drug Haul Seized from Fishing Boat in Caspian Sea
item.description: During special operations in the Caspian Sea in October, 126 offenders were detained and 44 small watercraft were confiscated. The National Security Committee reported that 11.5 kg of narcotics and 88 km of poaching nets were found. Over 2,337 sturgeon and other fish were released back into their natural habitat.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Raise Minimum Wage, Invest Trillions in Infrastructure
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev announced a minimum wage increase to 110,000 tenge and the allocation of 6.5 trillion tenge from the National Fund for infrastructure projects. Kazakhstan aims for energy self-sufficiency by 2029. Micro and small businesses will be exempt from inspections for three years.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Economic Success Not Driven by Russia, Says National Bank Head
item.description: International investors view Kyrgyzstan's close ties with Russia as a risk due to sanctions. National Bank Chairman Almaz Baketaev stated that while Russia is a partner, it's not the main driver of Kyrgyzstan's economic success. Sanctions against Russia have provided Kyrgyzstan with an economic boost and increased cross-border trade.
